dedupe_keys.name: open multi attribute dataset of 382 virginia data centre facilities from satellite imagery and ai

description: Researchers at the University of Virginia, published on the university's LibraData repository in May 2026, give an open facility-level dataset of 382 data centres in Virginia, the world's largest data centre market. It is built with a modular pipeline called Data Center Satellite-based ENergy and Spatial Estimation, which combines remote sensing, computer vision, machine learning and statistical models. Each facility has 18 attributes: footprint and geometry, construction year, IT whitespace and built-out power capacity, three 24-hour power profiles, and proximity to electrical, transport, water and residential infrastructure. Detections agree with two independent facility registries (Pearson r above 0.99) and construction years are within one bin for 86.4 percent of facilities. Coverage: Virginia, United States. Format and access: tabular and geospatial files on LibraData, free of charge; the licence is set on the repository page (not read). Caveats: capacities and power profiles are model estimates, not operator data; one state. Simulation uses: data centre loads for grid planning and cascading failure studies between power and digital infrastructure, and exposure of facilities to hazards and water stress. Related records: the Virginia DEQ data centre air permit index, the IM3 data centre load projections and commercial inventories such as the 451 Research knowledge base.
